samples.summary: New nonce plumbing in `GitHubAuthGuard` (query capture + 1..128 length bound) has no test at all
samples.evidence: The guard now reads `req.query.nonce` and stores it only when `typeof nonce === 'string' && length > 0 && length <= MAX_NONCE_LENGTH` (github-auth.guard.ts:26-38). There is no `github-auth.guard.spec.ts` — `ls packages/backend/src/auth/*.spec.ts` yields auth.controller, cli-auth.store, auth.service, jwt.strategy, github.strategy only — and a repo-wide grep for `GitHubAuthGuard` in tests returns nothing. The controller spec exercises the echo by calling `cliAuthStore.createState('cli', 9876, 'n0nce-x/y')` directly (auth.controller.spec.ts:220), bypassing the guard entirely. So the middle link of the chain (browser query → stored state) is untested: dropping the nonce read, inverting the length check, or accepting an array-valued `?nonce=` would keep every suite green.

samples.summary: No test asserts the CLI actually sends `&nonce=` on the OAuth start URL it later gates on
samples.evidence: login.ts:42-46 mints the nonce and appends `&nonce=<enc>` to the OAuth URL; the callback server then rejects any callback that does not echo it (login.ts:206). The only new CLI test, test/login-callback.test.ts, calls `startCallbackServer('the-nonce')` in isolation and never drives `registerLoginCommand`'s action. If the `&nonce=` param were dropped or misnamed, the backend would echo no `state`, the CLI would 400 its own genuine callback and hang until the 30s timeout — and both the new CLI test and the backend controller test (which seeds the nonce into the store directly) would still pass.

samples.summary: Nonce-mismatch coverage only exercises the length-differs branch, so a length-only comparison would pass
samples.evidence: `nonceMatches` (login.ts:164-169) is `a.length === b.length && timingSafeEqual(a, b)`. The test's two rejection cases are no state at all and `state=guessed` (7 chars) against `the-nonce` (9 chars) — both short-circuit on the length check, so `timingSafeEqual` is never reached with a mismatching same-length value. Replacing the body with `return a.length === b.length` (accepting any 9-char attacker state) leaves the suite green. A same-length wrong-value case (e.g. `state=xxx-nonce`) is what would pin the actual comparison.

samples.summary: No test pins the no-nonce branch of the state echo (`stateEcho === ''`)
samples.evidence: The controller conditionally appends `&state=` only when `state.nonce` is set. The pre-existing test at auth.controller.spec.ts:205 asserts only `stringMatching(/^http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:9876\/callback\?code=.+/)`, which matches whether or not a stray `state` param is appended, and the new test only covers the nonce-present case. Nothing fails if the empty-nonce branch emitted `&state=undefined`.

samples.summary: The `command: commandPath(this)` wiring into the orchestrators (files upload/download, docs/notes/slides import) is never asserted end-to-end
samples.evidence: Five call sites now pass `command: commandPath(this)` into runFilesUpload/runFilesDownload/runDocsImport/runNotesImport/runSlidesImport. Grepping packages/cli/test for `error.command` / `'files.upload'` / `'docs.import'` shows assertions only for docs.get, docs.content, sheets.cells.get, schema and the synthetic `boom` command; the orchestrator unit tests (files-upload.test.ts, docs-import.test.ts, notes-import.test.ts, slides-import.test.ts, files-download.test.ts) all invoke the run* functions directly without `command`, so they assert the un-attributed shape. A typo or omitted field in any of those five wirings would ship silently.

finding.summary: New nonce plumbing in `GitHubAuthGuard` (query capture + 1..128 length bound) has no test at all
finding.evidence: The guard now reads `req.query.nonce` and stores it only when `typeof nonce === 'string' && length > 0 && length <= MAX_NONCE_LENGTH` (github-auth.guard.ts:26-38). There is no `github-auth.guard.spec.ts` — `ls packages/backend/src/auth/*.spec.ts` yields auth.controller, cli-auth.store, auth.service, jwt.strategy, github.strategy only — and a repo-wide grep for `GitHubAuthGuard` in tests returns nothing. The controller spec exercises the echo by calling `cliAuthStore.createState('cli', 9876, 'n0nce-x/y')` directly (auth.controller.spec.ts:220), bypassing the guard entirely. So the middle link of the chain (browser query → stored state) is untested: dropping the nonce read, inverting the length check, or accepting an array-valued `?nonce=` would keep every suite green.

verdict.reason: The guard logic is present exactly as described (github-auth.guard.ts:6, 22-45: query capture of `nonce` plus a `length > 0 && length <= MAX_NONCE_LENGTH` bound), and no test anywhere in the repo exercises it. Repo-wide greps for `GitHubAuthGuard|github-auth.guard` return only the source, the `@UseGuards` site (auth.controller.ts:83), the module provider (auth.module.ts:30), and a string path inside an unrelated review-adapter fixture (scripts/agent/eval/adapters/coderabbit.test.mjs:96) that never instantiates the guard. There is no github-auth.guard.spec.ts, and I enumerated every backend spec/test/e2e-spec file including the full packages/backend/test/ e2e suite — none issues a request to /auth/github (only integration-helpers.ts:93 sets the callback env var). The closest coverage, auth.controller.spec.ts:217-223, seeds the nonce by calling cliAuthStore.createState('cli', 9876, 'n0nce-x/y') directly and drives the callback with query:{state}, so the guard is bypassed; cli-auth.store.spec.ts never passes a nonce at all (all createState calls are two-arg). Consequently deleting the nonce read, inverting the length check, or accepting an array-valued ?nonce= would keep all suites green. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a real behavior change with no meaningful test — major, blocking. I found no counterexample.

finding.summary: No test asserts the CLI actually sends `&nonce=` on the OAuth start URL it later gates on
finding.evidence: login.ts:42-46 mints the nonce and appends `&nonce=<enc>` to the OAuth URL; the callback server then rejects any callback that does not echo it (login.ts:206). The only new CLI test, test/login-callback.test.ts, calls `startCallbackServer('the-nonce')` in isolation and never drives `registerLoginCommand`'s action. If the `&nonce=` param were dropped or misnamed, the backend would echo no `state`, the CLI would 400 its own genuine callback and hang until the 30s timeout — and both the new CLI test and the backend controller test (which seeds the nonce into the store directly) would still pass.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: login.ts:42-46 mints a nonce and appends `&nonce=<enc>` to the OAuth start URL, and login.ts:203-210 gates the callback on that nonce being echoed back as `state`. No test anywhere asserts the outgoing URL carries the nonce. The only new CLI test (test/login-callback.test.ts:9-35) imports just `startCallbackServer` and passes a literal 'the-nonce', exercising the gate half only. Repo-wide greps for `nonce=`, `mode=cli`, `oauthUrl`, `Opening browser`, `auth/github`, and importers of `commands/login` produced no test hits — only src files and design docs. The only program-level touchpoint, output.test.ts:628-644, merely asserts 'login' is among registered command names; namespaces/schema/version tests likewise only inspect command metadata and never run the action, and no test mocks `open`. Backend auth.controller.spec.ts:217 seeds the nonce into the store directly, so it cannot catch a dropped or misnamed CLI query param. Both halves would stay green while real login 400s its own callback and hangs to the 30s timeout — a clear behavior change with no meaningful test (major under the missing-tests part of the test-adequacy lane).

finding.summary: Nonce-mismatch coverage only exercises the length-differs branch, so a length-only comparison would pass
finding.evidence: `nonceMatches` (login.ts:164-169) is `a.length === b.length && timingSafeEqual(a, b)`. The test's two rejection cases are no state at all and `state=guessed` (7 chars) against `the-nonce` (9 chars) — both short-circuit on the length check, so `timingSafeEqual` is never reached with a mismatching same-length value. Replacing the body with `return a.length === b.length` (accepting any 9-char attacker state) leaves the suite green. A same-length wrong-value case (e.g. `state=xxx-nonce`) is what would pin the actual comparison.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. nonceMatches (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:164-169) is `!received -> false` then `a.length === b.length && timingSafeEqual(a, b)`, and it is the sole gate at login.ts:206. The only test covering it, packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts:10-35, uses expected nonce 'the-nonce' (9 chars) with rejection probes of (a) no state — short-circuits at the `!received` guard, and (b) state=guessed (7 chars) — short-circuits at the length check. Neither reaches timingSafeEqual with a same-length mismatching value, so replacing the body with `return a.length === b.length` keeps the suite green. That mutant is a real bypass, not a hypothetical: the nonce is randomBytes(32).toString('base64url') (login.ts:42), always 43 chars, so a length-only compare accepts any 43-char attacker state — the exact attack the test's header comment cites (RFC 8252 8.9). Searched wide for a counterexample: repo-wide grep for startCallbackServer|the-nonce|callback\?code|Invalid state matches only login.ts and login-callback.test.ts (rest are docs prose); repo-wide grep for state=|nonce surfaces no other CLI test; packages/cli/test/**/*.test.ts enumerated with no other login/auth test. The nearest neighbour, packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.spec.ts:217-230, only asserts the backend echoes the nonce into the redirect URL and never invokes the CLI comparison, so it is not a counterexample. Blocking under the test-adequacy rubric: the discriminating half of a security-critical comparison ships with no test that can fail if it breaks.

finding.summary: New nonce ingestion in GitHubAuthGuard has no test at all
finding.evidence: The guard now reads `req.query.nonce` and applies real validation logic (must be a string, non-empty, <= MAX_NONCE_LENGTH=128) before forwarding it to `cliAuthStore.createState`. Grepping the backend for `GitHubAuthGuard`/`github-auth.guard` returns only auth.controller.ts, auth.module.ts and the guard itself — there is no `github-auth.guard.spec.ts` (only auth.controller, auth.service, jwt.strategy, github.strategy, cli-auth.store specs exist). So nothing covers: nonce forwarded on the happy path, an over-length nonce being dropped, an array-valued `?nonce=a&nonce=b` query (Express gives an array — `typeof !== 'string'` → undefined, silently disabling the binding check), or an empty nonce. This is the entry point of the whole anti-code-injection chain and it is entirely untested; the controller test only exercises the store→redirect half.

verdict.reason: The guard does real, branching validation of the CLI nonce: github-auth.guard.ts:26-39 reads req.query.nonce and forwards it to cliAuthStore.createState only when typeof nonce === 'string' && length > 0 && length <= MAX_NONCE_LENGTH (128, line 6), else passes undefined. A repo-wide grep for github-auth / GitHubAuthGuard / __cliStateToken / MAX_NONCE returns only auth.controller.ts:24,91, auth.module.ts:9, github.strategy.ts:59 and the guard itself (other hits are .agent-review artifacts and an unrelated eval fixture in scripts/agent/eval/adapters/coderabbit.test.mjs:96). The backend spec/e2e file list contains no guard spec, and no e2e test hits /auth/github?mode=cli (grep for 'auth/github|mode=cli' only hits packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:46 and a callback-URL constant in packages/backend/test/helpers/integration-helpers.ts:93). Nearby tests cover only the other halves: auth.controller.spec.ts constructs the controller directly (lines 42-47) so the guard never runs, and its nonce test (line 217-220) seeds the store itself via createState('cli', 9876, 'n0nce-x/y'); cli-auth.store.spec.ts never passes a nonce (all createState calls are 2-arg, lines 16-101); packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts covers only the CLI-side callback match. So the guard's ingestion branches (happy path, over-length drop, array-valued ?nonce=a&nonce=b, empty string) have no test anywhere.
